question: What is the principal layout difference between the pathway grade crossing and the sidewalk grade crossing in Figure 8E-1?
model_answer: Direct Answer: In Figure 8E-1, the principal layout difference is the relationship of the crossing to a roadway. Panel A (pathway grade crossing) shows the pathway crossing the tracks alone within its own "Pathway right-of-way," independent of any roadway, while Panel B (sidewalk grade crossing) shows the sidewalk running parallel to and immediately adjacent to a roadway, with both contained within the "Highway right-of-way." In both panels the crossing passes through the railroad right-of-way and detectable warnings are placed across the full width of the pathway or sidewalk on each approach. Standards (mandatory): - "Detectable warnings (see Chapter 3C) shall be used at pathway grade crossings where pedestrian travel is permitted and at sidewalk grade crossings and shall extend across the full width of the pathway or sidewalk." (This requirement applies to both configurations shown in Figure 8E-1, and the detectable warnings are depicted on both panels.) Visual evidence: [Image 5] shows Figure 8E-1 on page 1035, with Panel A ("Pathway grade crossing") depicting a stand-alone pathway in its own pathway right-of-way crossing the tracks, and Panel B ("Sidewalk grade crossing") depicting a sidewalk alongside a roadway, both within a single highway right-of-way, with detectable warnings marked on each approach in both panels; the accompanying Section 8E.01 text on the same page explains that a pathway is frequently placed in its own right-of-way independent of any roadway, whereas a sidewalk runs parallel to a roadway within the highway right-of-way close enough that the roadway crossing's traffic control devices can influence sidewalk users. [Image 4] (Figure 8E-2) further illustrates the sidewalk-type arrangement in which the sidewalk crossing lies adjacent to the roadway and its warning devices. Citations: - Section 8E.04 Standard §7 (p.1038) - Page 1076 - Figure 8E-2 (p.1036)
gold_answer: The pathway crossing is on a separate pathway alignment outside the roadway, whereas the sidewalk crossing is part of the highway corridor alongside the roadway and crosses the tracks with the roadway.
